Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through
quiz.answers_at: Answers. One: fifty plus seventy minus forty

questions.q: Receivables are 50, inventory 70, payables 40. What is operating working capital?
Inventory days 30, receivable days 20, payable days 60. What's the cash conversion cycle?
questions.explain: 30 + 20 − 60 = −10 days: the company is paid ten days before it pays its suppliers.
questions.explain_at: Say the café holds stock for ten days

questions.q: Inventory goes up by 15. What happens to cash?
questions.explain: More stock on the shelf is cash spent but not yet back. Working capital up, cash down.
questions.explain_at: If working capital goes up, cash goes down

questions.q: Payables go up by 10. What happens to cash?
questions.explain: You've kept your suppliers' money for longer, so cash is 10 higher. It isn't free, though: suppliers push back.

questions.q: Why can a fast-growing, profitable company run out of cash?

options.text: More sales bring more cash straight away
Fast growth raises the tax bill first
Growth ties up cash before profit arrives

questions.explain: Receivables and inventory grow with sales and absorb cash before the profit turns into cash. Bankers call it growing broke.
questions.explain_at: Third trap, and it kills real companies
